patches.why: SetTextureBudget x4: Low 3 GiB, Medium 6 GiB, High 12 GiB. For 16 GB+ cards (e.g. RTX 4080/4090, RX 7900).
Mip-requirement throttle: load 1.0 (0x1414df178) instead of 0.25: every object and level re-evaluated every frame.
.data qword 0x141e54d48 (5000 ms, single reader 0x1405b9d16 in resolver 0x1405b9ba0): after the cache was last <=16 MiB from full, mip upgrades resume after 1000 ms instead of 5000 ms.

evidence: Graphics-apply 0x140d8a9c0 maps settings quality.textures (local [rbp+0xf], from quality struct +0x48) to: Low -> SetTexMaxLog2A(10)/B(11)/SetTextureBudget(0x30000000=768 MiB); Medium -> 11/12/0x60000000=1.5 GiB; High -> 16/16/0xC0000000=3 GiB (0x140d8ac20..0x140d8ac90). SetTextureBudget 0x1405998e0 clamps to [32 MiB, 64 GiB] and stores global 0x141edeb10; only callers are those 3 sites. Texture cache copies it to cache+0x168 (0x140563b03 init, 0x1405772ba per-frame). Per-frame cache update 0x140577070: free = budget - used (used = 0x141ed7918, a soft counter adjusted by per-texture resident sizes [tex+0xd0] at 0x140538a87/0x14057a340/0x1405b1d5b - no up-front reservation); pressure flag cache+0x162 = (free/budget <= 0.05, const 0x1414dc854); if free <= 16 MiB, cache+0x150 = now. Request resolver 0x1405b9ba0 (called once from 0x1405bcb22): under pressure queues up to 16 mip DOWNGRADES per call; mip UPGRADES (max 4 per call) only once (now - cache+0x150) >= 5000 ms (.data qword 0x141e54d48 = 5000, single reader 0x1405b9d16). So when the 3 GiB High budget fills, high mips are dropped and no upgrade happens until 5 s after memory frees: the 'stuck at low detail' symptom. Separately, 'Calculate Object Mip Requirements' 0x140569320 re-evaluates only max(80, round(0.25*objects)) objects and max(1, round(0.25*levels)) levels per frame (shared const 0.25 at 0x1414e5c54 loaded once into xmm2 at 0x140569433 for both). NOT verified in game: frame-time cost, real VRAM use, WDDM behaviour when the budget exceeds the card's VRAM.
risk: Use only on 16 GB+ VRAM: a 12 GiB High budget can exceed smaller cards and cause WDDM paging/stutter or D3D12 allocation failures. Full per-frame requirement sweep costs ~4x the stock CPU time for that job. Shorter upgrade freeze can make a genuinely full cache thrash (upgrade -> evict) instead of settling. Mutually exclusive with perf_streaming (same bytes for the first two patches). Nothing written to saves.
